programme: No single nameable module. The twelve factors sit in at least six unrelated regulatory systems: CTCFL is the testis-restricted CTCF paralog acting as a chromatin insulator and cancer-testis antigen; HOXA11 is a homeobox developmental/EMT transcription factor; E2F7 is an atypical, repressive E2F that dampens CDKN1A/VEGFA-linked cell-cycle and angiogenic genes; COPS5 is a COP9-signalosome subunit that controls CDKN1B (p27) turnover; TRERF1 spans steroidogenic genes (CYP11A1, CYP17A1) and immune-checkpoint genes (FOXP3, CD80/86, LILRBs); MECP2 is a methyl-CpG chromatin reader central to Rett-syndrome neurobiology; ZNF350 is a BRCA1-partnered DNA-damage repressor; SRSF2 is a core spliceosome component linked to mitotic kinases (AURKA/B); PAX5 is the B-lymphocyte lineage master regulator; EGR4 is a neuroendocrine immediate-early gene; EWSR1 is an RNA-binding protein best known as a sarcoma fusion partner; RCOR2 is a CoREST-family corepressor for neuronal gene silencing. These do not share a complex, a pathway, or even a tissue logic — a developmental homeobox factor, a B-cell lineage TF, a splicing factor, and a Rett-syndrome chromatin reader do not combine into one process.
role_in_a: Not established. None of the twelve factors has a recorded Open Targets association with Fibromyalgia, and the only two with any retrieved literature (MECP2, EWSR1) are discussed in contexts (Rett syndrome/autism/breast cancer; Ewing sarcoma) that do not touch fibromyalgia.
role_in_b: Fragmentary at best. SRSF2, PAX5, and EWSR1 carry non-trivial Open Targets composite percentiles (~0.81, ~0.81, ~0.96) in Kidney_Papillary_Cell_Carcinoma, consistent with a generic role in a proliferative/splicing-dysregulated tumor, but this is three isolated factors with no shared complex, not a programme the other nine belong to.
shared_axis: None can be written that the record supports. Chronic centralized pain (blood transcriptome) and papillary renal cell carcinoma (kidney tumor) have no established shared biology, and this factor list — spanning developmental, immune, splicing, DNA-repair, and neuronal-chromatin systems — gives no coherent route from one to the other.
reasoning: The factors do not resolve into a recognizable module even when grouped by function, and the concordance counts (47/56 down to 24/56) track individual factor recurrence, not a shared programme. Literature retrieval was essentially empty: only MECP2 and EWSR1 returned papers, and neither supports fibromyalgia or a cross-disease link; Open Targets is silent for both diseases on nine of twelve factors. Forcing a story here would mean explaining away B-cell development (PAX5), Rett-syndrome chromatin biology (MECP2), and steroidogenesis/immune checkpoints (TRERF1) as one axis, which the data do not justify.
support: PMID 38817223 — reports a case of Ewing sarcoma of the kidney histologically mimicking papillary renal cell carcinoma; this is a diagnostic differential for EWSR1-fusion sarcoma versus papillary RCC, not evidence that EWSR1 regulates papillary RCC biology or links it to fibromyalgia. No other PMIDs were provided in the material (MECP2's further papers were noted as retrieved but no identifiers were given, and they concern Rett syndrome, MECP2-duplication syndrome, autism, and breast cancer, none of which bear on this pair).
how_to_falsify: Take the subset of factors with any shared downstream target (e.g., CDKN1A/CDKN1B, reached by E2F7, COPS5, TRERF1, and EWSR1) and test whether their binding or target expression moves concordantly between matched fibromyalgia blood cohorts and papillary RCC tumor cohorts more than expected by chance (e.g., via independent ChIP or RNA-seq replication across cohorts distinct from the one used here). If no concordant, reproducible signal emerges — as the current single-cohort, largely unretrieved-literature record suggests — that confirms incoherence; a robust cross-cohort concordant signal at these shared targets would be the specific finding needed to overturn this verdict.
caveats: All 56 patient-group comparisons come from a single independent cohort pair (independent cohort pairs: 1), so this is internal subgroup consistency, not cross-cohort replication. The tissues compared (blood for fibromyalgia, kidney for papillary RCC) are anatomically and functionally unconnected. Tissue-generic exclusions removed factors (CREB5, TCF7, RUNX2/3, ETS2, ERG, BCL6, KLF6, LITAF, EBF1, ZBTB4, E2F3) that might otherwise have supplied a plausible kidney/immune narrative — their absence here is by design, not oversight. Twelve additional factors were single-patient-group artifacts and are correctly excluded. ReMap binding evidence covers only a minority of targets for a handful of factors, so even the concordance counts reflect target-list overlap more than confirmed direct regulation.
